pattern: Tool with process and navigation subpatterns

evidence: Description had strong WHAT, WHEN, and trigger keywords.
Body and reference repeated generic click/snapshot tutorials and hard-coded session refs.
No operational guardrail existed for sending, reacting, deleting, or shared workspace actions.
The owned reference and template were not linked with conditional loading guidance.
Unread counting and completeness claims were unsafe for Slack's virtualized UI.

changes: Added action-risk classification, read-state awareness, privacy minimization, and confirmation gates.
Added send-once verification and duplicate-prevention recovery for uncertain outcomes.
Removed stale numeric refs, brittle Slack CSS assumptions, raw snapshot reporting, and unsupported count claims.
Added search, thread-context, virtualized-list, identity-disambiguation, and permission-boundary playbooks.
Added explicit on-demand reference/template triggers and Do Not Load guidance.
Replaced the report template with scoped provenance, coverage, confirmation, verification, and redaction fields.

remaining_gaps: UI labels and Slack behavior can vary by workspace and Slack release.
No live authenticated Slack workspace was available for end-to-end interaction testing.
